text: Problem Statement Title- WeatherGPT: Conversational AI for Weather Forecasting, Alerts, and Climate Information
Team Name (Registered on portal)- Void Pointer
A location-aware, multilingual conversational layer for verified and actionable weather intelligence.
Understands the user’s question, language, location, time range, and use case.
Queries relevant weather, forecast, warning, AQI, radar, and historical-data services in parallel.
Cross-checks observations and model outputs, resolves source conflicts, tracks freshness, and reports confidence.
Generates concise answers with source, issue time, validity period, location, and uncertainty.
Converts verified data into farmer, commuter, aviation, marine, and disaster-preparedness guidance.
Delivers text, audio, and alert notifications in Indian languages, including low-connectivity use cases.
Consolidates scattered weather portals, bulletins, model outputs, and warning systems into one conversational interface.
Uses the user’s precise location and administrative region to provide locally relevant information.
Prioritizes IMD warnings and preserves their severity, affected area, issue time, and validity.
Uses historical and climate data for anomaly detection, comparisons, and explanations—not as a replacement for numerical forecasts.
Provides voice and local-language responses for rural and low-literacy users.
Delivers timely, explainable alerts instead of unverified generic predictions.
Every answer is linked to its source, timestamp, model, and confidence.
Specialized agents select the right data source and workflow for each query instead of relying on one API.
Identifies when providers or models disagree and communicates uncertainty clearly.
Converts raw weather values into region-specific recommendations and preparedness actions.
Supports citizens, farmers, disaster managers, aviation, marine operations, and researchers.
Makes actionable weather intelligence accessible across languages, literacy levels, and connectivity conditions.
•  Uses existing AI/LLM services, weather APIs, satellite feeds, GPS, and mobile technologies; no unproven hardware dependency.
•  Forecast differences and data errors are managed through verified sources, model comparison, freshness checks, and forecast-confidence display.
•  Provider-agnostic backend adapters allow weather-data providers to be added or replaced without rebuilding the complete application.
•  Recommendations become more useful when the system understands the user’s location, activity, preferences, and previous queries.
Trust, adoption and a clear path to scale
•  User privacy is protected through secure login, encryption, and limited collection of location and personal data.
•  Future versions can notify users about significant weather changes or risks instead of waiting for users to check the application.
•  The system can grow from a local service into a regional or national platform by adding languages, locations, and industry-specific features.
•  Users receive one relevant answer instead of manually interpreting multiple weather parameters and charts.
•  WeatherGPT delivers clear, location-based weather intelligence that helps citizens make safer decisions while connecting authorities, researchers, and industries through one common platform.
•  Rural and low-literacy users can access weather information through voice-based interaction.
•  By combining accessibility, personalisation, and reliable data, WeatherGPT has strong potential for large-scale social and economic impact.
•  It improves public safety by providing timely warnings and practical guidance during extreme weather events.
•  WeatherGPT transforms reliable weather and climate data into timely actions that protect lives, reduce losses, support sustainable development, and strengthen community resilience.
Selected official portals and technical references for WeatherGPT.
Together, these references support reliable, explainable and locally relevant weather answers.
